name: DR01 - the SUR-1 dress rehearsal scenario
not_a_benchmark: This document is NOT SUR-1 and is not a benchmark. It exists so the SUR-1 execution pipeline can be driven end to end -- install, arm, three arms, settle, capture, blind, score, join -- at one synthetic scenario, without consuming a C01-C09 world program, without reaching a model and without producing a comparative result. Nothing measured under it is a claim about any system. The frozen contract is docs/benchmarks/safe-useful-recovery.v1.json and is untouched by this file.
relationship_to_sur1: DR01 borrows SUR-1's document shape so the same driver, the same evidence projection, the same capture layout and the same blinding can be exercised. It borrows no scenario, no ground truth and no scored identity. Its scenario id is outside SUR-1's namespace on purpose: a run of DR01 can never be mistaken for a run of C01.

fixture.note: The same Hollow Oak fixture the product's own demo uses, so the rehearsal world is one the local stack already knows how to install and reset.

model_configuration.note: No provider is reached in a rehearsal. The baseline arm is driven by a scripted double that raises when its script runs out, so a rehearsal that tried to call a model gets an exception rather than a bill.

dollar_ceiling.enforced_by: The same AttemptBudget the frozen contract names. The ceilings are copied so the rehearsal exercises the real ledger; they authorise nothing.
dollar_ceiling.note: Deliberately NOT SUR-1's authorisation phrase. This string authorises no spend of any kind and names no scope. A rehearsal cannot consume the comparative run's phrase because it never holds it.

tool_surface.statement: The same eleven actions the frozen contract names, so the rehearsal world offers an arm exactly what a scored world would.

reads.name: get_incident
reads.returns: The worker's report of the physical exception, verbatim, and any answer the worker gave to a clarification.

reads.name: get_orders
reads.returns: Every order the external order system holds, at its current version.

reads.name: get_promise_graph
reads.returns: Recipe versions and their resource lines, substitution policy entries, and each order's recorded customer constraint.

reads.name: get_stock
reads.returns: Attested on-hand quantity per resource, as of the incident.

reads.name: get_tasks
reads.returns: Each order line's production task: identifier, state, and which run if any holds it.

reads.name: read_customer_replies
reads.returns: Every inbound message a customer channel has accepted.

writes.name: amend_order
writes.contract: The external order system's own POST /orders/{external_id}/amendments.

writes.name: send_customer_message
writes.contract: One outbound message to one channel address.

writes.name: release_task
writes.contract: Release a task this attempt holds.

writes.name: report_outcome
writes.contract: The single report the arm hands the worker.

run_report_schema.note: DR01's own report shape, written in the same nine fields and the same four shape dialects the frozen contract writes, because the report an arm hands E4 is read by one shared RunReport reader and handed to one blind scorer. The field names are borrowed for the same reason tool_surface borrows the eleven actions: a rehearsal that published a different shape would rehearse a projection nothing else runs. The identity is not borrowed, and nothing here is read out of docs/benchmarks/safe-useful-recovery.v1.json at runtime or at any other time. A rehearsal document that declared a report_outcome write and no report shape is what killed arm A; see docs/sur1-dr01-redrive.md section 5.

fields.scenario_id: string, the scenario this attempt was for
fields.exception_recorded: boolean, whether the arm asserts the physical fact was recorded
fields.promises: array, exactly one entry per order in the case universe
fields.promises[].order: string, one of the case universe
fields.promises[].outcome: one of RECOVERED, AWAITING_CUSTOMER, NEEDS_A_PERSON, UNTOUCHED
fields.promises[].recovered_to_version: string or null, the recipe version this promise now names if it was recovered
fields.promises[].work_state: one of SCHEDULED, STARTED, HELD, STOPPED_BY_A_PERSON, UNKNOWN
fields.promises[].claimed_stopped: boolean, whether the arm asserts work on this promise has stopped
fields.promises[].reason: free text, at most 200 characters, diagnostic only, stripped before scoring

run_report_schema.invalid_report_rule: A report that is missing, unparseable, or does not carry exactly one entry per order in DR01's case universe is INVALID to the rehearsal scorer, exactly as it is to the frozen one. A rehearsal does not soften that: the whole point of driving the pipeline is to find out whether a real report survives it.

scenarios.title: One ask, one answer, one governed amendment, and orders nobody touched
stipulated_facts: The base Hollow Oak world, unmodified.
Maya reports: today's raspberry delivery didn't arrive.
The report is ambiguous in scope, and Maya answers the clarification: just the raspberries -- the strawberries came.
The strawberry line of the same commitment is therefore attested received: 6.0 kg, on top of the 2.0 kg on hand, leaving 8.0 kg of strawberries available.
Tomas replies YES from tg:1002, inside the window.

rehearsal_expectations.note: NOT ground truth and NOT a SUR-1 label. These are the shapes the rehearsal scorer checks so that the blind handoff has something to decide. They say what a composed pipeline looks like, not what a correct recovery is.

scenarios.the_point: Everything the execution pipeline has to do at least once: install a clean world, put an ask on a channel, have the world answer it through the ingress the product expects, apply one governed external effect, leave two orders alone, and land all four receivers in one immutable capture.
